guo2020.title: Accelerating large-scale inference with anisotropic vector quantization
guo2020.how: read page text via zsearch show (Zotero full text)
guo2020.use: Exact (flat) search compares the query with every stored vector, so one query costs O(n*d); a lookup-table quantizer cuts it to O(kd + n). (Sec. 4, PDF p.5) | ScaNN's anisotropic quantization loss penalizes the quantization error parallel to a data point more than the orthogonal error, because parallel error distorts high inner products. (Sec. 1 contributions, PDF p.1) | +1 more in claims.json

douze2024.title: The Faiss library
douze2024.how: read page text via zsearch show (Zotero full text)
douze2024.use: Faiss's IndexFlat is plain brute-force search; branch-and-bound exact methods give no speed-up over it in high dimensions. (brute-force search paragraph, PDF p.4) | Faiss recommends non-exhaustive (approximate) search once a collection is larger than about 10,000 vectors. (Sec. 5, PDF p.9) | +6 more in claims.json

annbenchmarks2026.title: ANN-Benchmarks live results: glove-100-angular (k = 10)

(glove-100-angular_10_angular.html, Recall/QPS chart data) | On the live glove-100-angular (k=10) results (April 2025, r6i.16xlarge, one CPU per run), the fastest at recall >= 0.9 are qsgngt (~7,560 QPS), NGT-qg (~5,460) and ScaNN (~5,180); hnswlib reaches ~780 and pgvector ~70. (README.md (run note) + glove-100-angular_10_angular.html chart data) | +1 more in claims.json

jegou2011.title: Product quantization for nearest neighbor search
jegou2011.how: read page text via zsearch show (Zotero full text)
jegou2011.use: Product quantization splits each D-dimensional vector into m sub-vectors of D/m dimensions and quantizes each sub-vector with its own small k-means codebook. (Sec. II-B, PDF p.4 (Zotero PDF = INRIA preprint; PDF page = printed page + 1)) | The PQ authors suggest 256 centroids per sub-quantizer (8 bits each) and m = 8 sub-vectors, i.e. a 64-bit (8-byte) code per vector. (Sec. II-B, PDF p.5 (Zotero PDF = INRIA preprint; PDF page = printed page + 1)) | +9 more in claims.json

malkov2018.title: Efficient and robust approximate nearest neighbor search using Hierarchical Navigable Small World graphs
malkov2018.how: read page text via zsearch show (Zotero full text)
malkov2018.use: HNSW is a stack of proximity graphs over nested subsets of points; each point's top layer is drawn at random with exponentially decaying probability. (Abstract, PDF p.1) | Search starts at the top (sparse, long links) layer, greedily descends, and restarts on each lower layer from the previous layer's local minimum. (Sec. 3, PDF p.3) | +5 more in claims.json

subramanya2019.title: DiskANN: Fast accurate billion-point nearest neighbor search on a single node
subramanya2019.how: read page text via zsearch show (Zotero full text)
subramanya2019.use: DiskANN indexes and serves one billion points on one workstation with 64 GB RAM and an inexpensive SSD. (Abstract, PDF p.1) | On SIFT1B, DiskANN serves over 5,000 queries per second at under 3 ms mean latency and 95%+ 1-recall@1 on a 16-core machine; comparable-memory IVF-PQ methods plateau near 50%. (Abstract, PDF p.1) | +5 more in claims.json

aumuller2020.title: ANN-Benchmarks: A benchmarking tool for approximate nearest neighbor algorithms
aumuller2020.how: read page text via zsearch show (Zotero full text)
aumuller2020.use: ANN-Benchmarks defines recall as the share of the k returned points that are within the distance of the true k-th nearest neighbour (equal to the intuitive set overlap when distances are distinct). (Sec. 2, PDF p.4) | ANN-Benchmarks runs each algorithm on a single CPU thread by default, to compare implementations on equal ground. (Sec. 3, PDF p.7) | +2 more in claims.json

shakir2024.title: Binary and scalar embedding quantization for significantly faster & cheaper retrieval
shakir2024.how: read the blog page via defuddle; month of publication unverified (year 2024 from the blog's citation block)
shakir2024.use: Binary quantization keeps one bit per dimension (threshold at 0), a 32x memory and storage reduction versus float32; distances become Hamming distances. (Binary Quantization section) | Rescoring (retrieve 4x top-k with binary codes, then re-rank with the float32 query) raised mxbai-embed-large-v1 from about 92.5% to about 96% of float32 retrieval quality. (Binary Quantization + Binary Rescoring sections) | +3 more in claims.json

kusupati2022.title: Matryoshka Representation Learning
kusupati2022.how: read page text via zsearch show (Zotero full text)
kusupati2022.use: Matryoshka Representation Learning trains one embedding so that its first m dimensions are themselves a usable embedding, optimizing O(log d) nested sizes. (Sec. 1, PDF p.2) | The paper's '14x' figures are on ImageNet image models: 14x smaller representation for the same classification accuracy, and 14x wall-clock (128x FLOPs) faster adaptive retrieval; they are not text-retrieval results. (Abstract, PDF p.1; Sec. 4.3.1, PDF p.8)

vault2026.title: EmbeddingGemma-2 - Evaluation for the Thesis (vault note, pilot)
vault2026.how: read the vault note; this is a small pilot (n=40, one LLM judge), provisional, not a primary publication

patel2024.title: ACORN: Performant and predicate-agnostic search over vector embeddings and structured data
patel2024.how: read page text via zsearch show (Zotero full text)
patel2024.use: Pre-filtering finds all records that pass the predicate and brute-forces them: perfect recall, but cost grows linearly with selectivity times dataset size, O(sn + K). (Sec. 3.2, PDF p.3) | Post-filtering searches the ANN index, drops non-matching results and must widen the search; when matching vectors are far from the query it degrades to O(n). (Sec. 3.2, PDF p.3) | +2 more in claims.json

gollapudi2023.title: Filtered-DiskANN: Graph algorithms for approximate nearest neighbor search with filters
gollapudi2023.how: read the authors' PDF (harsha-simhadri.org/pubs/Filtered-DiskANN23.pdf, 11 pp.) via pypdf; Zotero item KZGA5HCX has no full text
gollapudi2023.use: Filtered-DiskANN builds label-aware Vamana graphs (FilteredVamana, StitchedVamana) that handle about 1,000 labels and are an order of magnitude or more faster than prior filtered-search baselines. (Abstract, p.1) | Post-processing a normal ANN index works poorly for rare labels: many candidates may be retrieved before one matches the filter. (Sec. 1, p.2)

pgvector2026.title: pgvector README: Filtering and Iterative Index Scans
pgvector2026.how: read raw README.md from GitHub master
pgvector2026.use: In pgvector, HNSW filtering is applied after the index scan: with the default ef_search of 40 and a filter matching 10% of rows, only about 4 rows return; iterative index scans (since 0.8.0) scan further. (README, Filtering section)

qdrant2026.title: Qdrant documentation: Indexing (Filterable HNSW Index)
qdrant2026.how: read the docs page via defuddle
qdrant2026.use: Qdrant adds extra HNSW edges per indexed payload field (filterable HNSW) because strict filters make the plain graph fall apart; combined strict filters can still disconnect it, so v1.16 added ACORN search. (Indexing page, Filterable HNSW Index section)

robertson2009.how: read PDF page via zsearch show (Zotero full text)
robertson2009.use: BM25 scores a document by summing, over the query terms, a term weight that combines a saturating term-frequency part with an idf-like (RSJ) part. (Sec. 3.4, Eq. 3.15, printed p. 360 (PDF p. 30)) | The parameter b sets document-length normalisation: b = 1 is full normalisation and b = 0 switches it off. (Sec. 3.4.5, Eq. 3.12, printed p. 359 (PDF p. 29)) | +4 more in claims.json

(Sec. 1.1, printed p. 6 (PDF p. 31)) | The index is built in advance: collect documents, tokenise, normalise the tokens, then index each term with its documents. elastic2026.title: Language analyzers (Elasticsearch reference, current docs)
elastic2026.how: read official docs page (current version) via defuddle

apache2024.title: PersianNormalizer (Lucene 9.12.0 analysis-common API docs)
apache2024.use: Lucene's Persian normaliser folds Farsi yeh and yeh barree to Arabic yeh, keheh to Arabic kaf, and heh+hamza / heh goal forms to heh, so the two keyboard spellings of a word match. (Class PersianNormalizer, class description)

sqlite2026.title: SQLite FTS5 Extension (documentation)

thakur2021.title: BEIR: A Heterogeneous Benchmark for Zero-shot Evaluation of Information Retrieval Models
thakur2021.how: read PDF page via zsearch show (Zotero full text) (arXiv v4)
thakur2021.use: BEIR collects 18 public datasets from diverse retrieval tasks and domains and evaluates 10 retrieval systems (lexical, sparse, dense, late-interaction, re-ranking) zero-shot. (Abstract, p. 1) | BM25 is a strong zero-shot baseline in BEIR: it trails neural models by 7-18 points in-domain on MS MARCO but generally beats many more complex models out of domain. muennighoff2023.title: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
muennighoff2023.how: read PDF page via zsearch show (Zotero full text) (arXiv version)
muennighoff2023.use: In MTEB, a retrieval task has a corpus, queries and query-to-relevant-document labels; queries and documents are embedded and ranked by cosine similarity, and nDCG@10 is the main metric; the retrieval datasets come from BEIR. (Sec. 3.2 Tasks and evaluation, p. 4) | MTEB found that no single text-embedding method was best across all tasks. (Abstract, p. 1)

formal2021.title: SPLADE: Sparse Lexical and Expansion Model for First Stage Ranking
formal2021.how: read PDF page via zsearch show (Zotero full text)
formal2021.use: SPLADE predicts a weight for every vocabulary term from BERT's masked-language-model head and applies a log-saturation, w_j = sum over input tokens of log(1 + ReLU(w_ij)), which stops some terms dominating and yields sparsity. (Sec. 3, Eq. 4, p. 2) | SPLADE trains with a FLOPS regulariser (sum over terms of the squared mean activation), with separate weights for queries and documents, so the posting lists stay short and balanced. (Sec. 3, Eqs. 5-6, p. 3) | +2 more in claims.json

formal2021b.title: SPLADE v2: Sparse Lexical and Expansion Model for Information Retrieval
formal2021b.how: read arXiv PDF via pdfmd cache (markitdown; two-column text interleaved, numbers read from the table row)
formal2021b.use: SPLADE v2 replaces sum pooling with max pooling and adds distillation and hard negatives; DistilSPLADE-max reached MRR@10 0.368 on MS MARCO dev and nDCG@10 0.729 on TREC DL 2019. (Sec. 3 and Table 1 (6-page arXiv version))

khattab2020.title: ColBERT: Efficient and Effective Passage Search via Contextualized Late Interaction over BERT
khattab2020.how: read PDF page via zsearch show (Zotero full text)
khattab2020.use: ColBERT encodes the query and the document separately into one vector per token and scores them by late interaction: for each query vector take the maximum similarity over document vectors (MaxSim), then sum. (Sec. 3.1, p. 4) | Reranking BM25's top-1000 on MS MARCO, ColBERT reached MRR@10 34.9 (dev) at 61 ms and 7B FLOPs per query, vs BERT-base 34.7 at 10,700 ms and 97T FLOPs: over 170x faster with 14,000x fewer FLOPs. (Sec. 1, p. 2; Table 1, p. 7) | +1 more in claims.json

santhanam2022.title: ColBERTv2: Effective and Efficient Retrieval via Lightweight Late Interaction
santhanam2022.how: read PDF page via zsearch show (Zotero full text) (arXiv v1)
santhanam2022.use: ColBERTv2 stores each token vector as the id of its nearest centroid plus a 1- or 2-bit-per-dimension residual: 20 or 36 bytes per 128-d vector instead of ColBERT's 256 bytes. (Sec. 3.3, p. 4) | ColBERTv2's MS MARCO index needs 16 GiB (1 bit) or 25 GiB (2 bits) versus 154 GiB for ColBERT, a 6-10x reduction, about the size of a 768-d single-vector index. (Sec. 5.3, p. 9) | +1 more in claims.json

cormack2009.title: Reciprocal Rank Fusion Outperforms Condorcet and Individual Rank Learning Methods
cormack2009.how: read PDF page via zsearch show (Zotero full text)
cormack2009.use: Reciprocal Rank Fusion scores each document as the sum over rankings of 1/(k + rank), with k = 60 fixed in a pilot study; it needs no scores and no training. (Sec. 1, p. 1) | In the pilot runs k = 60 was near-optimal but not critical, and the constant k damps the effect of a high rank given by one outlier system. (Sec. 1, p. 1) | +1 more in claims.json

bruch2023.title: An Analysis of Fusion Functions for Hybrid Retrieval
bruch2023.how: read PDF page via zsearch show (Zotero full text)
bruch2023.use: Bruch et al. found that RRF is sensitive to its parameters and that a tuned convex combination alpha*f_sem + (1 - alpha)*f_lex beats RRF in- and out-of-domain, needs only a few labelled examples to tune alpha, and is largely insensitive to the choice of score normalisation. (Abstract, p. 1; Eq. for f_Convex, p. 6) | Because RRF uses only ranks, it ignores how far apart the raw scores are, which discards useful information. (Sec. 1, p. 2)

nogueira2019.title: Passage Re-ranking with BERT
nogueira2019.how: read PDF page via zsearch show (Zotero full text)
nogueira2019.use: A BERT cross-encoder reads the query and passage together (up to 512 tokens) and outputs a relevance probability; each passage of BM25's top-1000 is scored independently, i.e. one forward pass per (query, passage) pair. (Sec. 2, p. 2) | Reranking BM25's top-1000, BERT-large reached MS MARCO MRR@10 36.5 (dev) and 35.8 (eval), vs 16.7 / 16.5 for untuned Lucene BM25. (Table 1, p. 3)

baai2024r.title: BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3 (Hugging Face model card)
baai2024r.how: read the Hugging Face model card via defuddle

edge2024.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization
edge2024.how: read PDF page via zsearch show (Zotero full text) (arXiv v2)
edge2024.use: GraphRAG's index is built by an LLM: it extracts entities, relationships and claims from text chunks, then partitions the graph with hierarchical Leiden community detection. (pp. 4-5 (pipeline description)) | GraphRAG pre-writes a summary for every community; a global question is answered by map-reduce: each community summary gives a partial answer, and the partial answers are summarised into one final answer. (Sec. 1, p. 2) | +2 more in claims.json

guo2024.title: LightRAG: Simple and Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation
guo2024.how: read PDF page via zsearch show (Zotero full text)
guo2024.use: LightRAG indexes an LLM-built entity-relation graph by text key-value pairs: each key is a word or short phrase, each value a summary paragraph; retrieval works at a low level (specific entities) and a high level (broader themes). (p. 3 (LLM Profiling for Key-Value Pair Generation); p. 2) | LightRAG claims it uses under 100 tokens and one API call for retrieval, against GraphRAG's 610 x 1,000 tokens on the Legal dataset, and can add new text without rebuilding the index. (Fig. 2 table and text, p. 9)

gutierrez2024.title: HippoRAG: Neurobiologically Inspired Long-Term Memory for Large Language Models
gutierrez2024.how: read PDF page via zsearch show (Zotero full text)

(Sec. 1, p. 2) | Single-step HippoRAG matched or beat iterative IRCoT retrieval while being 6-13x faster and 10-20x (or 10-30x, by version) cheaper. (Abstract, p. 1)
